questions.text: The relation $R=\{(x, y): x, y\in\mathbf{Z} \text{ and } x+y \text{ is even}\}$ is:
options: reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
questions.sol:
Reflexive: $x+x=2x$ is even.
Symmetric: $x+y=y+x$.
Transitive: if $x+y$ and $y+z$ are even, then $x+z=(x+y)+(y+z)-2y$ is even.
So $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: If $f(x)=\dfrac{2^x}{2^x+\sqrt{2}}$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{81}f\left(\frac{k}{82}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$f(1-x)=\dfrac{2^{1-x}}{2^{1-x}+\sqrt2}=\dfrac{2}{2+\sqrt2\cdot2^x}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt2+2^x}$, so $f(x)+f(1-x)=1$.
Pair $k$ with $82-k$ for $k=1,\ldots,40$: 40 pairs give 40. The middle term is $f\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2}=\dfrac12$.
Sum $=40+\dfrac12=\dfrac{81}{2}$.

questions.text: Let O be the origin, the point A be $z_1=\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}i$, the point B $(z_2)$ be such that $\sqrt{3}|z_2|=|z_1|$ and $\arg(z_2)=\arg(z_1)+\dfrac{\pi}{6}$. Then
options: ABO is an obtuse angled isosceles triangle
questions.sol:
$OA=|z_1|=\sqrt{3+8}=\sqrt{11}$, $OB=\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt3}$ and $\angle AOB=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
$AB^2=11+\dfrac{11}{3}-2\cdot\sqrt{11}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt3}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\dfrac{11}{3}$, so $AB=OB$: the triangle is isosceles.
$OA^2=11>OB^2+AB^2=\dfrac{22}{3}$, so the angle at B is obtuse.
(Area $=\dfrac12\cdot\sqrt{11}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt3}\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac{11}{4\sqrt3}$, which matches neither area option.)

questions.text: The sum, of the squares of all the roots of the equation $x^2+|2x-3|-4=0$, is
questions.sol:
$x\ge\dfrac32$: $x^2+2x-7=0 \Rightarrow x=-1\pm2\sqrt2$; only $x=2\sqrt2-1\approx1.83$ is valid.
$x<\dfrac32$: $x^2-2x-1=0 \Rightarrow x=1\pm\sqrt2$; only $x=1-\sqrt2$ is valid.
Sum of squares $=(9-4\sqrt2)+(3-2\sqrt2)=12-6\sqrt2=6(2-\sqrt2)$.

questions.text: Let $<a_n>$ be a sequence such that $a_0=0$, $a_1=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $2a_{n+2}=5a_{n+1}-3a_n$, $n=0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{100}a_k$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The characteristic equation $2r^2-5r+3=0$ has roots $1$ and $\dfrac32$, so $a_n=A+B\left(\dfrac32\right)^n$.
$a_0=0$ and $a_1=\dfrac12$ give $B=1$, $A=-1$: $a_n=\left(\dfrac32\right)^n-1$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{100}a_k=\dfrac{\frac32\left(\left(\frac32\right)^{100}-1\right)}{\frac12}-100=3\left(\left(\tfrac32\right)^{100}-1\right)-100=3a_{100}-100$.

questions.text: Let $T_r$ be the $r^{\text{th}}$ term of an A.P. If for some m, $T_m=\dfrac{1}{25}$, $T_{25}=\dfrac{1}{20}$, and $20\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{25}T_r=13$, then $5m\displaystyle\sum_{r=m}^{2m}T_r$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{25}T_r=\dfrac{25}{2}(T_1+T_{25})=\dfrac{13}{20} \Rightarrow T_1+T_{25}=\dfrac{26}{500}$, so $T_1=\dfrac{1}{500}$.
$d=\dfrac{T_{25}-T_1}{24}=\dfrac{1}{500}$, hence $T_r=\dfrac{r}{500}$.
$T_m=\dfrac{1}{25}=\dfrac{20}{500} \Rightarrow m=20$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=20}^{40}T_r=\dfrac{1}{500}\cdot\dfrac{21(20+40)}{2}=\dfrac{630}{500}$, and $5m\cdot\dfrac{630}{500}=100\cdot\dfrac{630}{500}=126$.

questions.text: The number of different 5 digit numbers greater than 50000 that can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, such that the sum of their first and last digits should not be more than 8, is
questions.sol:
The first digit is 5, 6 or 7 (repetition allowed).
First 5: last digit 0-3 (4 ways); first 6: 0-2 (3 ways); first 7: 0-1 (2 ways). That is 9 choices of first and last digits.
The middle three digits: $8^3=512$ ways. Total $9\times512=4608$.
This includes 50000 itself, which is not greater than 50000, so the answer is $4608-1=4607$.

questions.text: Two number $k_1$ and $k_2$ are randomly chosen from the set of natural numbers. Then, the probability that the value of $i^{k_1}+i^{k_2}$, $(i=\sqrt{-1})$ is non-zero, equals
questions.sol:
Only the remainders of $k_1, k_2$ on division by 4 matter, and each of the 16 pairs of remainders is equally likely.
$i^{k_1}+i^{k_2}=0$ exactly when $i^{k_2}=-i^{k_1}$, i.e. $k_2\equiv k_1+2 \pmod 4$: 4 of the 16 pairs.
Probability of a non-zero value $=1-\dfrac{4}{16}=\dfrac34$.

questions.text: Let ABCD be a trapezium whose vertices lie on the parabola $y^2=4x$. Let the sides AD and BC of the trapezium be parallel to y-axis. If the diagonal AC is of length $\dfrac{25}{4}$ and it passes through the point $(1, 0)$, then the area of ABCD is
questions.sol:
$(1,0)$ is the focus, so AC is a focal chord with ends $(t^2,2t)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{t^2},-\dfrac{2}{t}\right)$; its length is $\left(t+\dfrac1t\right)^2=\dfrac{25}{4}$, so $t=2$.
A $(4,4)$, C $\left(\dfrac14,-1\right)$. AD and BC are vertical chords: D $(4,-4)$, B $\left(\dfrac14,1\right)$.
Parallel sides $AD=8$ and $BC=2$, distance between them $4-\dfrac14=\dfrac{15}{4}$.
Area $=\dfrac12(8+2)\cdot\dfrac{15}{4}=\dfrac{75}{4}$.

questions.text: Let ${}^nC_{r-1}=28$, ${}^nC_r=56$ and ${}^nC_{r+1}=70$. Let A $(4\cos t, 4\sin t)$, B $(2\sin t, -2\cos t)$ and C $(3r-n, r^2-n-1)$ be the vertices of a triangle ABC, where t is a parameter. If $(3x-1)^2+(3y)^2=\alpha$, is the locus of the centroid of triangle ABC, then $\alpha$ equals
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{{}^nC_r}{{}^nC_{r-1}}=\dfrac{n-r+1}{r}=2$ and $\dfrac{{}^nC_{r+1}}{{}^nC_r}=\dfrac{n-r}{r+1}=\dfrac54$ give $n=8$, $r=3$. So C is $(1,0)$.
Centroid: $3x-1=4\cos t+2\sin t$, $3y=4\sin t-2\cos t$.
$(3x-1)^2+(3y)^2=16+4=20$ (the cross terms cancel). So $\alpha=20$.

questions.text: Let the equation of the circle, which touches x-axis at the point $(a, 0)$, $a>0$ and cuts off an intercept of length b on y-axis be $x^2+y^2-\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0$. If the circle lies below x-axis, then the ordered pair $(2a, b^2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Below the x-axis and touching it at $(a,0)$: centre $(a,-r)$, so the circle is $x^2+y^2-2ax+2ry+a^2=0$.
Hence $\alpha=2a$, $\beta=2r$, $\gamma=a^2$.
On $x=0$: $y^2+2ry+a^2=0$; the intercept is $b=2\sqrt{r^2-a^2}$, so $b^2=4r^2-4a^2=\beta^2-4\gamma$.
$(2a,b^2)=(\alpha,\beta^2-4\gamma)$.

questions.text: $\cos\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}+\sin^{-1}\dfrac{5}{13}+\sin^{-1}\dfrac{33}{65}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Let $\theta=\sin^{-1}\dfrac35+\sin^{-1}\dfrac{5}{13}$. Then $\cos\theta=\dfrac45\cdot\dfrac{12}{13}-\dfrac35\cdot\dfrac5{13}=\dfrac{33}{65}$ (and $\theta$ is acute).
So $\theta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{33}{65}$, and $\theta+\sin^{-1}\dfrac{33}{65}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
The value is $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}=0$.

questions.text:
Let A $(x, y, z)$ be a point in $xy$- plane, which is equidistant from three points $(0, 3, 2)$, $(2, 0, 3)$ and $(0, 0, 1)$. Let B $=(1, 4, -1)$ and C $=(2, 0, -2)$. Then among the statements
(S1) : $\Delta ABC$ is an isosceles right angled triangle, and
(S2) : the area of $\Delta ABC$ is $\dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}$,
questions.sol:
With $z=0$: equal distances from $(0,3,2)$ and $(0,0,1)$ give $-6y+13=1$, $y=2$; from $(2,0,3)$ and $(0,0,1)$ give $-4x+13=1$, $x=3$. So A $=(3,2,0)$.
$\vec{AB}=(-2,2,-1)$, $\vec{AC}=(-1,-2,-2)$: both have length 3 and $\vec{AB}\cdot\vec{AC}=2-4+2=0$.
So the triangle is right-angled and isosceles (S1 true), with area $\dfrac12\cdot3\cdot3=\dfrac92$ (S2 false).

questions.text: If the image of the point $(4, 4, 3)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{3}$ is $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to
questions.sol:
A point of the line is $F(1+2t, 2+t, 1+3t)$. $\vec{PF}=(2t-3, t-2, 3t-2)$ must be perpendicular to $(2,1,3)$: $14t-14=0$, $t=1$.
Foot $F=(3,3,4)$, so the image is $2F-P=(2,2,5)$.
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=9$.

questions.text:
The sum of all local minimum values of the function
$f(x)=\begin{cases}1-2x, & x<-1\\ \dfrac{1}{3}(7+2|x|), & -1\le x\le2\\ \dfrac{11}{18}(x-4)(x-5), & x>2\end{cases}$
is
questions.sol:
$f$ decreases on $x<0$ (from $1-2x$, then $\dfrac{7-2x}{3}$), increases on $[0,2]$ to $\dfrac{11}{3}$, and for $x>2$ the parabola starts at $\dfrac{11}{18}\cdot2\cdot3=\dfrac{11}{3}$ and has its vertex at $x=\dfrac92$.
Local minima: $x=0$ with $f=\dfrac73$, and $x=\dfrac92$ with $f=\dfrac{11}{18}\cdot\dfrac12\cdot\left(-\dfrac12\right)=-\dfrac{11}{72}$. ($x=2$ is a local maximum.)
Sum $=\dfrac{168-11}{72}=\dfrac{157}{72}$.

questions.text: The area (in sq. units) of the region $\{(x, y): 0\le y\le2|x|+1,\ 0\le y\le x^2+1,\ |x|\le3\}$ is
questions.sol:
$x^2+1\le2|x|+1 \iff |x|\le2$, so the upper boundary is $x^2+1$ for $|x|\le2$ and $2|x|+1$ for $2\le|x|\le3$.
By symmetry, area $=2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^2(x^2+1)\,dx+\int_2^3(2x+1)\,dx\right]=2\left[\dfrac{14}{3}+6\right]=\dfrac{64}{3}$.

questions.text: Let for some function $y=f(x)$, $\displaystyle\int_0^x t\,f(t)\,dt=x^2f(x)$, $x>0$ and $f(2)=3$. Then $f(6)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Differentiate: $xf(x)=2xf(x)+x^2f'(x)$, so $x^2f'(x)=-xf(x)$, i.e. $\dfrac{f'}{f}=-\dfrac1x$.
Hence $f(x)=\dfrac{c}{x}$; $f(2)=3$ gives $c=6$.
$f(6)=1$.

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a function defined by $f(x)=(2+3a)x^2+\left(\dfrac{a+2}{a-1}\right)x+b$, $a\neq1$. If $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+1-\dfrac{2}{7}xy$, then the value of $28\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5}|f(i)|$ is
questions.sol:
For $f(x)=Ax^2+Bx+b$: $f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y)=2Axy-b$. Comparing with $1-\dfrac27xy$: $A=-\dfrac17$, $b=-1$.
$2+3a=-\dfrac17 \Rightarrow a=-\dfrac57$, so $B=\dfrac{a+2}{a-1}=\dfrac{9/7}{-12/7}=-\dfrac34$.
$f(x)=-\dfrac{x^2}{7}-\dfrac{3x}{4}-1$, negative for $x>0$, so $|f(i)|=\dfrac{i^2}{7}+\dfrac{3i}{4}+1$.
$28\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5}|f(i)|=28\left(\dfrac{55}{7}+\dfrac{45}{4}+5\right)=220+315+140=675$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{96x^2\cos^2x}{(1+e^x)}\,dx=\pi(\alpha\pi^2+\beta)$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{Z}$, then $(\alpha+\beta)^2$ equals
questions.sol:
For even $g$, $\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a}\frac{g(x)}{1+e^x}dx=\int_0^a g(x)\,dx$ (add the integral with $x\to-x$).
So $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}96x^2\cos^2x\,dx=48\int_0^{\pi/2}x^2(1+\cos2x)\,dx$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x^2dx=\dfrac{\pi^3}{24}$ and $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x^2\cos2x\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^2\sin2x}{2}+\dfrac{x\cos2x}{2}-\dfrac{\sin2x}{4}\right]_0^{\pi/2}=-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
$I=2\pi^3-12\pi=\pi(2\pi^2-12)$: $\alpha=2$, $\beta=-12$, $(\alpha+\beta)^2=100$.

questions.text:
Let M denote the set of all real matrices of order $3\times3$ and let $S=\{-3, -2, -1, 1, 2\}$. Let
$S_1=\{A=[a_{ij}]\in M: A=A^T \text{ and } a_{ij}\in S, \forall\, i, j\}$,
$S_2=\{A=[a_{ij}]\in M: A=-A^T \text{ and } a_{ij}\in S, \forall\, i, j\}$,
$S_3=\{A=[a_{ij}]\in M: a_{11}+a_{22}+a_{33}=0 \text{ and } a_{ij}\in S, \forall\, i, j\}$.
If $n(S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3)=125\,\alpha$, then $\alpha$ equls ______.
questions.sol:
$S_2=\varnothing$: a skew-symmetric matrix has zero diagonal, and $0\notin S$.
$n(S_1)=5^6$ (diagonal and upper triangle free).
Diagonals from $S$ with sum 0: $\{-3,1,2\}$ (6 orders), $\{-2,1,1\}$ (3), $\{-1,-1,2\}$ (3), i.e. 12. So $n(S_3)=12\cdot5^6$ and $n(S_1\cap S_3)=12\cdot5^3$.
$n=5^6+12\cdot5^6-12\cdot5^3=125(13\cdot125-12)=125\cdot1613$, so $\alpha=1613$.

questions.text: If $\alpha=1+\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{6}(-3)^{r-1}\,{}^{12}C_{2r-1}$, then the distance of the point $(12, \sqrt{3})$ from the line $\alpha x-\sqrt{3}y+1=0$ is______.
questions.sol:
In $(1+i\sqrt3)^{12}=\displaystyle\sum_k {}^{12}C_k(i\sqrt3)^k$, the odd terms $k=2r-1$ give $i\sqrt3\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{6}(-3)^{r-1}\,{}^{12}C_{2r-1}$.
$(1+i\sqrt3)^{12}=2^{12}(\cos4\pi+i\sin4\pi)=2^{12}$ is real, so the sum is 0 and $\alpha=1$.
Distance of $(12,\sqrt3)$ from $x-\sqrt3y+1=0$: $\dfrac{|12-3+1|}{2}=5$.

questions.text: Let $E_1: \dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$ be an ellipse. Ellipses $E_i$'s are constructed such that their centres and eccentricities are same as that of $E_1$, and the length of minor axis of $E_i$ is the length of major axis of $E_{i+1}$ $(i\ge1)$. If $A_i$ is the area of the ellipse $E_i$, then $\dfrac{5}{\pi}\left(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}A_i\right)$, is equal to ____.
questions.sol:
Same eccentricity means $b_i=\dfrac23a_i$, and $a_{i+1}=b_i=\dfrac23a_i$, with $a_1=3$.
$A_i=\pi a_ib_i=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}a_i^2$, and $a_i^2$ is a G.P. with first term 9 and ratio $\dfrac49$.
$\displaystyle\sum A_i=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\cdot\dfrac{9}{1-\frac49}=\dfrac{54\pi}{5}$, so $\dfrac5\pi\sum A_i=54$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{d}=\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=|\vec{c}|$, $|\vec{c}-2\vec{a}|^2=8$ and the angle between $\vec{d}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then $|10-3\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}|+|\vec{d}\times\vec{c}|^2$ is equal to _____.
questions.sol:
$|\vec c|^2-4\vec a\cdot\vec c+12=8$ with $\vec a\cdot\vec c=|\vec c|$ gives $(|\vec c|-2)^2=0$, so $|\vec c|=2$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec c=2$.
$\vec d=(-1,1,0)$, $|\vec d|=\sqrt2$: $\vec d\cdot\vec c=\sqrt2\cdot2\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=2$ and $|\vec d\times\vec c|^2=2\cdot4\cdot\dfrac12=4$.
With $\vec c=(c_1,c_2,c_3)$: $c_2=c_1+2$, $c_3=2-c_1-c_2=-2c_1$, and $|\vec c|^2=6c_1^2+4c_1+4=4$, so $c_1=0$ or $-\dfrac23$.
$\vec b\cdot\vec c=2+(c_1+c_2)$ is 4 or $\dfrac83$; in both cases $|10-3\vec b\cdot\vec c|=2$.
Value $=2+4=6$.

questions.text:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}3x, & x<0\\ \min\{1+x+[x],\ x+2[x]\}, & 0\le x\le2\\ 5, & x>2,\end{cases}$
where [.] denotes greatest integer function. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the number of points, where f is not continuous and is not differentiable, respectively, then $\alpha+\beta$ equals____.
questions.sol:
On $[0,1)$: $\min\{1+x, x\}=x$. On $[1,2)$: $\min\{2+x, x+2\}=x+2$. At $x=2$: $\min\{5,6\}=5$.
$x=0$: continuous ($f\to0$), but slopes 3 and 1 differ, so not differentiable.
$x=1$: left limit 1, $f(1)=3$: discontinuous. $x=2$: left limit 4, $f(2)=5$: discontinuous.
$\alpha=2$, $\beta=3$, so $\alpha+\beta=5$.

questions.text: The center of mass of a thin rectangular plate (fig - x) with sides of length $a$ and $b$, whose mass per unit area $(\sigma)$ varies as $\sigma=\dfrac{\sigma_0x}{ab}$ (where $\sigma_0$ is a constant), would be ______
questions.sol:
$\sigma$ depends only on $x$, so by symmetry $y_{cm}=\dfrac{b}{2}$.
$x_{cm}=\dfrac{\int_0^a x\cdot x\,dx}{\int_0^a x\,dx}=\dfrac{a^3/3}{a^2/2}=\dfrac{2a}{3}$.
Centre of mass: $\left(\dfrac{2a}{3}, \dfrac{b}{2}\right)$.

questions.text: A bead of mass 'm' slides without friction on the wall of a vertical circular hoop of radius 'R' as shown in figure. The bead moves under the combined action of gravity and a massless spring (k) attached to the bottom of the hoop. The equilibrium length of the spring is 'R'. If the bead is released from top of the hoop with (negligible) zero initial speed, velocity of bead, when the length of spring becomes 'R', would be (spring constant is 'k', g is accleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
At the top the spring length is $2R$, so its extension is $R$; when its length is $R$ the extension is zero.
A chord of length $R$ from the bottom of the circle reaches a height $\dfrac{R^2}{2R}=\dfrac{R}{2}$, so the bead falls $2R-\dfrac{R}{2}=\dfrac{3R}{2}$.
Energy: $\dfrac12kR^2+mg\cdot\dfrac{3R}{2}=\dfrac12mv^2 \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{3Rg+\dfrac{kR^2}{m}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: In a central force field, the work done is independent of the path chosen.
Reason R: Every force encountered in mechanics does not have an associated potential energy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
A central force $F(r)\hat{r}$ is conservative, so the work done between two points does not depend on the path: A is true.
Not every force has a potential energy (friction, for example, is non-conservative): R is true.
R is a general remark and does not explain why a central force is conservative, so it is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider following statements:
A. Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the interior as compared to the molecules at the surface, of a liquid.
B. As the temperature of liquid rises, the coefficient of viscosity increases.
C. As the temperature of gas increases, the coefficient of viscosity increases
D. The onset of turbulence is determined by Reynold's number.
E. In a steady flow two stream lines never intersect.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A is false: the molecules at the surface (not the interior) have extra energy.
B is false: the viscosity of a liquid falls as the temperature rises.
C is true for gases. D is true: Reynolds number decides the onset of turbulence. E is true: two streamlines cannot cross, or the velocity at the crossing point would not be unique.
Answer: C, D, E only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In the experiment for measurement of viscosity '$\eta$' of given liquid with a ball having radius R, consider following statements.
A. Graph between terminal velocity V and R will be a parabola.
B. The terminal velocities of different diameter balls are constant for a given liquid.
C. Measurement of terminal velocity is dependent on the temperature.
D. This experiment can be utilized to assess the density of a given liquid.
E. If balls are dropped with some initial speed, the value of $\eta$ will change.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$V=\dfrac{2R^2(\rho-\sigma)g}{9\eta}$.
A: $V\propto R^2$, a parabola: true. B: $V$ depends on $R$: false.
C: $\eta$, and hence $V$, depends on temperature: true. D: with $\eta$ known, the same relation gives the liquid density $\sigma$: true.
E: the terminal velocity, and $\eta$, do not depend on the initial speed: false.
Answer: A, C and D only.

questions.text: For a particular ideal gas which of the following graphs represents the variation of mean squared velocity of the gas molecules with temperature?
questions.sol:
$\dfrac12m\overline{v^2}=\dfrac32k_BT$, so $\overline{v^2}=\dfrac{3k_BT}{m}\propto T$.
The correct graph is the straight line through the origin.

questions.text: A Carnot engine (E) is working between two temperatures 473K and 273K. In a new system two engines - engine $E_1$ works between 473K to 373K and engine $E_2$ works between 373K to 273K. If $\eta_{12}$, $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ are the efficiencies of the engines E, $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively, then
questions.sol:
$\eta_{12}=1-\dfrac{273}{473}=\dfrac{200}{473}\approx0.423$.
$\eta_1=\dfrac{100}{473}\approx0.211$ and $\eta_2=\dfrac{100}{373}\approx0.268$, so $\eta_1+\eta_2\approx0.479$.
Hence $\eta_{12}<\eta_1+\eta_2$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: A sound wave has higher speed in solids than gases.
Reason R: Gases have higher value of Bulk modulus than solids.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
Sound travels much faster in solids than in gases: A is true.
Solids have far larger elastic moduli than gases (which are easily compressed), so R is false.
Answer: A is true but R is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is bent into an equilateral triangle and an identical wire is bent into a square. The ratio of resistance between the two end points of an edge of the triangle to that of the square is
questions.sol:
Triangle: one side $\dfrac{R}{3}$ in parallel with $\dfrac{2R}{3}$: $\dfrac{(R/3)(2R/3)}{R}=\dfrac{2R}{9}$.
Square: $\dfrac{R}{4}$ in parallel with $\dfrac{3R}{4}$: $\dfrac{3R}{16}$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{2/9}{3/16}=\dfrac{32}{27}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider a long thin conducting wire carrying a uniform current I. A particle having mass "M" and charge "q" is released at a distance "$a$" from the wire with a speed $v_o$ along the direction of current in the wire. The particle gets attracted to the wire due to magnetic force. The particle turns round when it is at distance $x$ from the wire. The value of $x$ is
[$\mu_0$ is vacuum permeability]
questions.sol:
Take the wire along $z$. With $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}$, the component of the magnetic force along the wire is $m\dfrac{dv_z}{dt}=qB\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, so $m\,dv_z=\dfrac{q\mu_0I}{2\pi}\dfrac{dr}{r}$.
The magnetic force does no work, so the speed stays $v_o$. At the turning point the radial velocity is zero, so $v_z=-v_o$.
$m(-v_o-v_o)=\dfrac{q\mu_0I}{2\pi}\ln\dfrac{x}{a} \Rightarrow x=ae^{-\frac{4\pi mv_o}{q\mu_0I}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Find the equivalent resistance between two ends of the following circuit
questions.sol:
Label the junctions P (left end), Q, S and T (right end), with $\dfrac r3$ between P-Q, Q-S and S-T.
The upper wire joins P to S and the lower wire joins Q to T, so P and S are one node and Q and T are the other.
All three resistors then lie between the same two nodes, in parallel: $R=\dfrac{r/3}{3}=\dfrac{r}{9}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle of mass 'm' and charge 'q' is fastened to one end 'A' of a massless string having equilibrium length $l$, whose other end is fixed at point 'O'. The whole system is placed on a frictionless horizontal plane and is initially at rest. If uniform electric field is switched on along the direction as shown in figure, then the speed of the particle when it crosses the x-axis is
questions.sol:
The force $qE$ along $+x$ swings the particle about O on a circle of radius $l$, from $60^\circ$ above the x-axis down to the x-axis.
Displacement along the field $=l-l\cos60^\circ=\dfrac{l}{2}$, so the work done is $\dfrac{qEl}{2}$.
$\dfrac12mv^2=\dfrac{qEl}{2} \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\dfrac{qEl}{m}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel to a battery. Charge-time graph is shown below for the two capacitors. The energy stored with them are $U_1$ and $U_2$, respectively. Which of the given statements is true?
questions.sol:
In parallel both capacitors reach the same voltage $V$, so the final charge $q=CV$ is larger for the larger capacitance.
From the graph, the $C_2$ curve levels off at the higher charge, so $C_2>C_1$.
$U=\dfrac12CV^2$, so $U_2>U_1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Three infinitely long wires with linear charge density $\lambda$ are placed along the x-axis, y-axis and z-axis respectively. Which of the following denotes an equipotential surface?
questions.sol:
For a long line charge, $V=-\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}\ln r+\text{constant}$, with $r$ the distance from the line.
Distances from the x, y and z axes: $\sqrt{y^2+z^2}$, $\sqrt{z^2+x^2}$, $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.
$V=-\dfrac{\lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\ln\left[(x^2+y^2)(y^2+z^2)(z^2+x^2)\right]+\text{constant}$, so $V$ is constant when the product is constant.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Due to presence of an em-wave whose electric component is given by $E=100\sin(\omega t-kx)$ NC$^{-1}$, a cylinder of length 200 cm holds certain amount of em-energy inside it. If another cylinder of same length but half diameter than previous one holds same amount of em-energy, the magnitude of the electric field of the corresponding em-wave should be modified as
questions.sol:
The energy density is proportional to $E_0^2$, and the energy held is (energy density) $\times$ (volume).
Half the diameter gives a quarter of the volume, so $E_0^2$ must be four times as large: $E_0=2\times100=200$ NC$^{-1}$.
So $E=200\sin(\omega t-kx)$ NC$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A hemispherical vessel is completely filled with a liquid of refractive index $\mu$. A small coin is kept at the lowest point (O) of the vessel as shown in figure. The minimum value of the refractive index of the liquid so that a person can see the coin from point E (at the level of the vessel) is _____.
questions.sol:
To reach E, at the level of the rim, the ray must leave the surface grazing it (angle of refraction $90^\circ$), so $\sin i=\dfrac1\mu$ at the surface.
A ray from O meets the surface at angle $i$ with $\tan i=\dfrac{d}{R}$, where $d\le R$ is the distance from the centre C; the largest possible $i$ is $45^\circ$ (at the edge B).
So $\dfrac1\mu\le\sin45^\circ$, i.e. $\mu\ge\sqrt2$. The minimum value is $\sqrt2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin prism $P_1$ with angle $4^\circ$ made of glass having refractive index 1.54, is combined with another thin prism $P_2$ made of glass having refractive index 1.72 to get dispersion without deviation. The angle of the prism $P_2$ in degrees is
questions.sol:
No net deviation: $(\mu_1-1)A_1=(\mu_2-1)A_2$.
$0.54\times4=0.72\times A_2 \Rightarrow A_2=3^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A proton of mass '$m_p$' has same energy as that of a photon of wavelength '$\lambda$'. If the proton is moving at non-relativistic speed, then ratio of its de Broglie wavelength to the wavelength of photon is.
questions.sol:
Let the common energy be $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.
Proton: $\lambda_p=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_pE}}$.
$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda}=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_pE}}\cdot\dfrac{E}{hc}=\dfrac1c\sqrt{\dfrac{E}{2m_p}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Choose the correct nuclear process from the below options
[p: proton, n: neutron, e$^-$: electron, e$^+$: positron, $\nu$ : neutrino, $\bar{\nu}$ : antineutrino]
questions.sol:
Charge conservation needs an electron (not a positron) when a neutron becomes a proton.
Lepton number: the electron has $+1$, so an antineutrino ($-1$) must be emitted.
$\mathrm{n}\to\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{e}^-+\bar\nu$ ($\beta^-$ decay).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following circuits has the same outpur as that of the given circuit?
questions.sol:
The upper AND gate gets A and $\bar B$; the lower AND gate gets A (the line that crosses over B) and B. The NOR gate then gives
$Y=\overline{A\bar B+AB}=\overline{A(\bar B+B)}=\bar A$.
A NAND gate with both inputs joined to A also gives $\bar A$, so that circuit (A into a NAND gate) is the answer.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a measurement, it is asked to find modulus of elasticity per unit torque applied on the system. The measured quantity has dimension of $[M^aL^bT^c]$. If $b=3$, the value of c is _____
questions.sol:
Modulus of elasticity: $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$. Torque: $[ML^2T^{-2}]$.
Ratio: $[M^0L^{-3}T^0]$, so $c=0$.
(Strictly the power of L is $-3$; the question's "$b=3$" gives only its size. Either way $c=0$.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A tiny metallic rectangular sheet has length and breadth of 5 mm and 2.5 mm, respectively. Using a specially designed screw gauge which has pitch of 0.75 mm and 15 divisions in the circular scale, you are asked to find the area of the sheet. In this measurement, the maximum fractional error will be $\dfrac{x}{100}$ where $x$ is ________ .
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two iron solid discs of negligible thickness have radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ and moment of intertia $I_1$ and $I_2$, respectively. For $R_2=2R_1$, the ratio of $I_1$ and $I_2$ would be $1/x$, where x = _____.
questions.sol:
Same material and (equal, small) thickness: $M\propto R^2$.
$I=\dfrac12MR^2\propto R^4$, so $\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}=\left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}$.
$x=16$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
The moment of inertia of a solid disc rotating along its diameter is 2.5 times higher than the moment of inertia of a ring rotating in similar way. The moment of inertia of a solid sphere which has same radius as the disc and rotating in similar way, is n times higher than the moment of inertia of the given ring. Here, n = _____.
Consider all the bodies have equal masses.
questions.sol:
Disc about a diameter: $\dfrac{MR^2}{4}$; ring of radius $r$ about a diameter: $\dfrac{Mr^2}{2}$.
$\dfrac{R^2}{4}=2.5\cdot\dfrac{r^2}{2} \Rightarrow r^2=\dfrac{R^2}{5}$.
Sphere: $\dfrac25MR^2$, so $n=\dfrac{\frac25R^2}{\frac{R^2}{10}}=4$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A double slit interference experiment performed with a light of wavelength 600 nm forms an interference fringe pattern on a screen with 10th bright fringe having its centre at a distance of 10 mm from the central maximum. Distance of the centre of the same 10th bright fringe from the central maximum when the source of light is replaced by another source of wavelength 660 nm would be______mm.
questions.sol:
$y_n=\dfrac{n\lambda D}{d}\propto\lambda$.
$y=10\times\dfrac{660}{600}=11$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In a multielectron atom, which of the following orbitals described by three quantum numbers will have same energy in absence of electric and magnetic fields?
A. $n=1, l=0, m_l=0$
B. $n=2, l=0, m_l=0$
C. $n=2, l=1, m_l=1$
D. $n=3, l=2, m_l=1$
E. $n=3, l=2, m_l=0$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
In a multielectron atom the orbital energy depends on both $n$ and $l$ (not on $m_l$ without external fields).
Only D and E share $n=3$, $l=2$ (both 3d orbitals), so they are degenerate. B (2s) and C (2p) differ in $l$.
Answer: D and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The molecules having square pyramidal geometry are
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{BrF_5}$: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair (sp$^3$d$^2$), square pyramidal.
$\mathrm{XeOF_4}$: 5 bonded atoms + 1 lone pair on Xe, square pyramidal.
$\mathrm{PCl_5}$ and $\mathrm{SbF_5}$ have 5 bond pairs and no lone pair: trigonal bipyramidal.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: What is the freezing point depression constant of a solvent, 50 g of which contain 1 g non volatile solute (molar mass 256 g mol$^{-1}$) and the decrease in freezing point is 0.40 K ?
questions.sol:
Molality $=\dfrac{1/256}{0.050}=\dfrac{1}{12.8}$ mol kg$^{-1}$.
$K_f=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{m}=0.40\times12.8=5.12$ K kg mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Ice and water are placed in a closed container at a pressure of 1 atm and temperature 273.15K. If pressure of the system is increased 2 times, keeping temperature constant, then identify correct observation from following
questions.note: The final key gives "The solid phase (ice) disappears completely". "The amount of ice decreases" describes the direction of the shift, but at a constant 273.15 K and 2 atm no ice can remain, so the key's option is the complete answer.
questions.sol:
Ice $\rightarrow$ water involves a decrease in volume (ice is less dense), so raising the pressure favours water (Le Chatelier) and lowers the melting point below 273.15 K.
The temperature is held at 273.15 K, which is now above the melting point at 2 atm, so ice cannot coexist with water: the ice melts completely (and the volume of the system decreases).
Answer: the solid phase (ice) disappears completely.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A weak acid HA has degree of dissociation x. Which option gives the correct expression of $(\mathrm{pH}-\mathrm{p}K_a)$?
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{HA\rightleftharpoons H^++A^-}$; with degree of dissociation $x$, $\dfrac{[\mathrm{A^-}]}{[\mathrm{HA}]}=\dfrac{x}{1-x}$.
$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p}K_a+\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{A^-}]}{[\mathrm{HA}]}$, so $\mathrm{pH}-\mathrm{p}K_a=\log\left(\dfrac{x}{1-x}\right)$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I
(Redox Reaction)		LIST-II
(Type of Redox Reaction)
A.$\mathrm{CH_{4(g)}+2O_{2(g)}\xrightarrow{\Delta}CO_{2(g)}+2H_2O_{(l)}}$I.Disproportionation reaction
B.$\mathrm{2NaH_{(s)}\xrightarrow{\Delta}2Na_{(s)}+H_{2(g)}}$II.Combination reaction
C.$\mathrm{V_2O_{5(s)}+5Ca_{(s)}\xrightarrow{\Delta}2V_{(s)}+5CaO_{(s)}}$III.Decomposition reaction
D.$\mathrm{2H_2O_{2(aq)}\xrightarrow{\Delta}2H_2O_{(l)}+O_{2(g)}}$IV.Displacement reaction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: methane and oxygen combine to give the products; NCERT classes this combustion as a combination redox reaction (II).
B: NaH breaks down into its elements: decomposition (III).
C: Ca displaces V from its oxide: displacement (IV).
D: in $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$, oxygen ($-1$) goes to $-2$ and $0$: disproportionation (I).
Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$[\mathrm{A}]_0$ / mol L$^{-1}$$t_{1/2}$ / min
0.100200
0.025100
For a given reaction $\mathrm{R\to P}$, $t_{1/2}$ is related to $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ as given in table.
Given: $\log2=0.30$
Which of the following is true?
A. The order of the reaction is $\dfrac12$.
B. If $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ is 1M, then $t_{1/2}$ is $200\sqrt{10}$ min
C. The order of the reaction changes to 1 if the concentration of reactant changes from 0.100 M to 0.500 M.
D. $t_{1/2}$ is 800 min for $[\mathrm{A}]_0=1.6$ M
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
For order $n$, $t_{1/2}\propto[\mathrm{A}]_0^{\,1-n}$. $\dfrac{200}{100}=\left(\dfrac{0.100}{0.025}\right)^{1-n}$, i.e. $2=4^{1-n}$, so $n=\dfrac12$: A is true.
B: $t_{1/2}=200\left(\dfrac{1}{0.1}\right)^{1/2}=200\sqrt{10}$ min: true.
C: the order does not change with concentration: false.
D: $t_{1/2}=200\left(\dfrac{1.6}{0.1}\right)^{1/2}=200\times4=800$ min: true.
Answer: A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The incorrect decreasing order of atomic radii is
questions.sol:
Radii decrease across a period and increase down a group.
Mg is below Be, so Mg is larger than Be: the order $\mathrm{Be>Mg>Al>Si}$ is incorrect. The other three orders are correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Consider the following elements In, Tl, Al, Pb, Sn and Ge.
The most stable oxidation states of elements with highest and lowest first ionisation enthalpies, respectively, are
questions.sol:
First ionisation enthalpies (kJ mol$^{-1}$): Ge 762, Pb 716, Sn 709, Tl 589, Al 577, In 558.
Highest: Ge, whose most stable oxidation state is +4 (the inert pair effect is weak for Ge).
Lowest: In, whose most stable oxidation state is +3.
Answer: +4 and +3.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Which of the following oxidation reactions are carried out by both $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ and $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ in acidic medium?
A. $\mathrm{I^-\to I_2}$
B. $\mathrm{S^{2-}\to S}$
C. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}\to Fe^{3+}}$
D. $\mathrm{I^-\to IO_3^-}$
E. $\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-}\to SO_4^{2-}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
In acidic medium both oxidants convert iodide to iodine, sulphide (H$_2$S) to sulphur and Fe$^{2+}$ to Fe$^{3+}$.
Iodide to iodate and thiosulphate to sulphate are reactions of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ in neutral or faintly alkaline solution, not of acidified dichromate.
Answer: A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider 'n' is the number of lone pair of electrons present in the equatorial position of the most stable structure of $\mathrm{ClF_3}$. The ions from the following with 'n' number of unpaired electrons are
A. $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$
B. $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$
C. $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$
D. $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$
E. $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{ClF_3}$ is T-shaped with both lone pairs in equatorial positions, so $n=2$.
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ (3d$^2$) 2; $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ (3d$^1$) 1; $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ (3d$^9$) 1; $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ (3d$^8$) 2; $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ (3d$^2$) 2.
Answer: A, D and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The metal ion whose electronic configuration is not affected by the nature of the ligand and which gives a violet colour in non-luminous flame under hot condition in borax bead test is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ (3d$^8$) has the configuration $t_{2g}^6e_g^2$ in an octahedral field whatever the ligand, strong or weak, so its electronic configuration does not depend on the ligand. ($\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$, 3d$^5$, can be high-spin or low-spin.)
In the borax bead test, nickel gives a violet bead in the oxidising (non-luminous) flame while hot, turning reddish brown on cooling.
So the ion is $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\mathrm{Et_2N{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}$ will undergo alkaline hydrolysis at a faster rate than $\mathrm{Et_2CH{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}$
Statement II: In $\mathrm{Et_2N{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}$, intramolecular substitution takes place first by involving lone pair of electrons on nitrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{Et_2NCH_2CH_2Cl}$ the nitrogen lone pair displaces chloride intramolecularly, forming a strained aziridinium ion, which hydroxide then opens quickly (neighbouring group participation).
The carbon analogue $\mathrm{Et_2CHCH_2CH_2Cl}$ has no such help and reacts by ordinary, slower substitution.
Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of stability of following carbocations is :
questions.sol:
C, the tropylium (cycloheptatrienyl) cation, is aromatic ($6\pi$ electrons) and is the most stable.
A (triphenylmethyl) is stabilised by three phenyl rings, more than B (diphenylmethyl) with two.
D is a simple secondary alkyl cation, the least stable.
Order: C > A > B > D.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
A molecule ("P") on treatment with acid undergoes rearrangement and gives ("Q"). ("Q") on ozonolysis followed by reflux under alkaline condition gives ("R"). The structure of ("R") is given below.
The structure of ("P") is
questions.note: Official final key: two options are accepted, 1-isopropylcyclopentanol and isopropenylcyclopentane (either is awarded marks). Both can give the same tertiary carbocation in acid, which rearranges by ring expansion to 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene (Q).
questions.sol:
R is 1-acetyl-2-methylcyclopentene, the intramolecular aldol product of octane-2,7-dione. That dione comes from ozonolysis of Q = 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene.
Isopropenylcyclopentane: protonation gives the tertiary cation $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C^+}$ next to the ring; ring expansion gives a cyclohexyl cation next to the $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_2}$ carbon; a methyl shift and loss of $\mathrm{H^+}$ give 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene.
1-Isopropylcyclopentanol: in acid it loses water to give a tertiary cation; a hydride shift to the side-chain cation and the same ring expansion and methyl shift also lead to 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The products A and B in the following reactions, respectively are
$\mathrm{A\xleftarrow{Ag-NO_2}CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Br\xrightarrow{AgCN}B}$
questions.sol: Silver salts are largely covalent, so the nucleophile attacks through its more electron-rich atom that is free: the nitrogen of $\mathrm{Ag{-}NO_2}$ gives the nitroalkane $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NO_2}$, and the nitrogen of AgCN gives the isocyanide $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NC}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Both acetaldehyde and acetone (individually) undergo which of the following reactions?
A. Iodoform Reaction
B. Cannizaro Reaction
C. Aldol Condensation
D. Tollen's Test
E. Clemmensen Reduction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Both contain $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$, so both give the iodoform test (A).
Both have $\alpha$-hydrogens, so both undergo aldol condensation (C) and neither gives the Cannizzaro reaction (B).
Only acetaldehyde gives Tollens' test (D). Both carbonyl groups are reduced to $\mathrm{CH_2}$ by Clemmensen reduction (E).
Answer: A, C and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The compounds that produce $\mathrm{CO_2}$ with aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution are:
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Only acids stronger than carbonic acid release $\mathrm{CO_2}$ from $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$.
A (benzoic acid) and D (cyclohexanecarboxylic acid) are carboxylic acids; C (2,4,6-trinitrophenol, picric acid) is strongly acidic because of the three nitro groups.
Phenol (B) and 4-methoxyphenol (E) are too weak.
Answer: A, C and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : D-glucose pentaacetate reacts with 2, 4 - dinitrophenylhydrazine
Statement II : Starch, on heating with concentrated sulfuric acid at $100^\circ$C and 2 - 3 atmosphere pressure produces glucose.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.note: The final key treats Statement II as true. NCERT describes boiling starch with dilute sulphuric acid at 393 K under 2-3 atm; on a strict reading of "concentrated" and "100 °C" Statement II could be judged false, which would make both statements false. The answer here follows the final key.
questions.sol:
Statement I: glucose pentaacetate has no free aldehyde group (the cyclic form is locked), so it does not react with 2,4-DNP or hydroxylamine: false.
Statement II: hydrolysis of starch with sulphuric acid under pressure (2-3 atm) gives glucose; this is how glucose is made from starch, and the final key treats the statement as true.
Answer (final key): Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the oxalic acid vs $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ (in the presence of dil $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) titration the solution needs to be heated initially to $60^\circ$C, but no heating is required in Ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) vs $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ titration (in the presence of dil $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$)
Statement II: In oxalic acid vs $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ titration, the initial formation of $\mathrm{MnSO_4}$ takes place at high temperature, which then acts as catalyst for further reaction. In the case of FAS vs $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$, heating oxidizes $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ into $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ by oxygen of air and error may be introduced in the experiment.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Oxalic acid reacts slowly with permanganate at first; warming to about $60^\circ$C starts the reaction, and the $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ formed then catalyses it (autocatalysis).
Fe$^{2+}$ reacts quickly at room temperature, and heating would let air oxidise some Fe$^{2+}$, causing an error.
Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The molarity of a 70% (mass/mass) aqueous solution of a monobasic acid (X) is _____ $\times10^{-1}$ M(Nearest integer)
[Given: Density of aqueous solution of (X) is 1.25 g mL$^{-1}$
Molar mass of the acid is 70 g mol$^{-1}$ ]
questions.sol:
1 L of solution has mass 1250 g, of which 70% is acid: 875 g $=\dfrac{875}{70}=12.5$ mol.
Molarity $=12.5$ M $=125\times10^{-1}$ M.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The formation enthalpies, $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ for $\mathrm{H_{(g)}}$ and $\mathrm{O_{(g)}}$ are 220.0 and 250.0 kJ mol$^{-1}$, respectively, at 298.15 K, and $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ for $\mathrm{H_2O_{(g)}}$ is $-242.0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ at the same temperature. The average bond enthalpy of the O-H bond in water at 298.15 K is_______ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{H_2O(g)\to2H(g)+O(g)}$: $\Delta H=2(220.0)+250.0-(-242.0)=932$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
This breaks two O-H bonds, so the average O-H bond enthalpy is $\dfrac{932}{2}=466$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below is the plot of the molar conductivity vs $\sqrt{\text{concentration}}$ for KCl in aqueous solution.
If, for the higher concentration of KCl solution, the resistance of the conductivity cell is 100 $\Omega$, then the resistance of the same cell with the dilute solution is 'x' $\Omega$
The value of x is ______ (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
From the plot: $\sqrt{c}=0.1$ ($c=0.01$) has $\Lambda_m=150$, and $\sqrt{c}=0.15$ ($c=0.0225$) has $\Lambda_m=100$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$.
$\kappa=\Lambda_mc$ and, for the same cell, $R\propto\dfrac1\kappa$.
$\dfrac{x}{100}=\dfrac{100\times0.0225}{150\times0.01}=\dfrac{2.25}{1.5}=1.5$, so $x=150$.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:
11.25 mg of chlorobenzene will produce ---- x10$^{-1}$ mg of product B.
(Consider the reactions result in complete conversion.)
[Given molar mass of C, H, O, N and Cl as 12, 1, 16, 14 and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl\xrightarrow{Mg}C_6H_5MgCl\xrightarrow{CO_2,\,H_3O^+}C_6H_5COOH\xrightarrow{NH_3,\,\Delta}C_6H_5CONH_2}$ (A).
Hoffmann bromamide degradation ($\mathrm{Br_2}$, NaOH) gives aniline, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$ (B, 93 g mol$^{-1}$).
11.25 mg $\div$ 112.5 g mol$^{-1}$ $=0.1$ mmol, giving $0.1\times93=9.3$ mg $=93\times10^{-1}$ mg.
